articles.headline: Could new Zim offer start bidding war?
articles.summary: An investor has submitted a surprise bid for ZIM Integrated Shipping Services that would increase the purchase price and keep the Israeli ocean carrier under Israeli control. The unsolicited offer raises the possibility of a bidding war for the liner. No financial terms of the competing bid were disclosed in the report.

articles.headline: Software vendor offers proposal to establish detention, demurrage accountability
articles.summary: A beneficial cargo owner technology provider has proposed a framework identifying 20 use cases under which shippers, consignees, and carriers can be held accountable for container detention and demurrage charges. The proposal is aimed at reducing costly dispute resolution between supply chain parties. The vendor's framework seeks to establish clear standards for assigning responsibility for container storage costs.

articles.headline: Guangzhou begins work on $2 billion fifth development phase at Nansha port
articles.summary: Construction has begun on a $2 billion fifth development phase at Nansha port in Guangzhou, China. The project includes four berths capable of handling vessels exceeding 21,000 TEUs, along with 15 berths for regional feeder vessels. The expansion represents a significant addition to one of China's major container port facilities.

articles.headline: US and China to establish trade board, tout agriculture commitments
articles.summary: The United States and China have announced plans to establish a trade board as part of ongoing bilateral trade negotiations. The two countries also highlighted agriculture commitments as part of the framework. Further details on the structure and scope of the trade board were included in the agreement announcement.

articles.headline: Parcel express services evolve as market fragmentation accelerates
articles.summary: Andy Dyer, CEO of transportation management firm AFS, which manages approximately $3 billion in parcel spend annually for its clients, says the parcel carrier market is experiencing accelerating fragmentation. Dyer notes the sector has undergone numerous disruptions, evolutions, and reinventions in recent years. The report examines how express parcel services are adapting to a market increasingly characterized by multiple competing carriers.

articles.headline: Industrial Realty Group, Sachem Capital Merge to Form $3.4B Industrial REIT
articles.summary: Industrial Realty Group (IRG), one of the largest private owners of U.S. industrial real estate, has agreed to merge with public mortgage trust Sachem Capital to form IRG Realty Trust, a $3.4 billion publicly traded real estate investment trust. The combined entity will bring together IRG's private industrial portfolio with Sachem Capital's public market structure. The merger creates a new publicly traded industrial REIT with a combined asset value of $3.4 billion.

articles.headline: Bond Traders See Shift Toward New Era of Higher Yields
articles.summary: A new era of elevated borrowing costs is potentially underway as war-driven inflation angst intensifies in the US bond market, sending 30-year yields toward a two-decade high above 5%, Bloomberg reported. Treasuries extended their slide Monday in Asia after their worst week in a year, with a renewed rally in oil adding to worries from reports showing inflation accelerated last month. The fear of resurgent price pressures roiled fixed-income globally, sparking a rout in markets including the UK and Japan. G-7 finance chiefs are set to discuss the debt selloff at their Paris meeting.

articles.headline: Latest Iran Offer on War Is Not Enough, Says White House
articles.summary: Hopes for a breakthrough in the US-Iran standoff over the closure of the Strait of Hormuz were dashed again on Monday after Iran delivered an updated peace proposal that the White House deemed insufficient. Earlier reports of a potential deal had fueled market optimism, but Wall Street's rebound attempt failed as stocks fell and Brent crude topped $110 per barrel in a volatile session. The S&P 500 erased earlier gains as oil extended its advance. The Strait of Hormuz has remained largely blocked since late February, cutting roughly 20% of global seaborne oil trade.

articles.headline: Oil Slips as Trump Spurs Optimism Over Iran Deal: Markets Wrap
articles.summary: Oil dropped in early Asia trading after President Donald Trump said he was holding off on fresh military strikes against Iran following appeals from Persian Gulf allies, boosting hopes for a deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to energy flows. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 1.4% after Trump said plans for a strike were called off, with the president adding that "serious negotiations are now taking place." S&P 500 futures were steady after the benchmark index had nearly wiped out its losses in a choppy Monday session. The Strait of Hormuz has remained largely closed since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in late February.

articles.headline: Oil Extends Gains as Trump Says Clock Is Ticking for Iran Deal
articles.summary: Oil rose for a third consecutive day on Monday as the US and Iran remained far apart on a deal to end weeks of war and reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude advanced above $110 a barrel, after adding almost 8% the prior week, while West Texas Intermediate rose above $107. President Trump posted on social media that "For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST," signaling his patience with Tehran was wearing thin. The International Energy Agency cautioned that oil inventories globally are depleting at a record pace as Hormuz remains closed.

articles.headline: LIRR Strike Inches Toward a Fourth Day as Talks Progress Slowly
articles.summary: The Long Island Rail Road strike approached a fourth day on Monday as labor groups and transit officials had yet to reach a deal, leaving the nation's busiest commuter rail line shuttered for the evening commute. Roughly 3,500 engineers, signalmen and electrical workers walked off the job on Saturday after negotiations between the state-run Metropolitan Transportation Authority and five union coalition members collapsed over wages and healthcare premiums. Parties restarted negotiations Sunday after failing to reach a deal by a late Friday deadline. The shutdown is the first LIRR work stoppage in more than 30 years, affecting over 250,000 daily commuters.

articles.headline: LIRR Strike Jams Roads, Prompts Long Commutes as Talks Continue
articles.summary: Long Island workers making their way into New York City grappled with long commutes Monday as the Long Island Rail Road entered its third strike day, the first weekday of the work stoppage. The LIRR — the nation's busiest commuter railroad — halted service on Saturday after roughly 3,500 engineers, signalmen and electrical workers walked off the job following a stalemate between the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and union leaders. Roads and alternative transit were strained across the region as commuters scrambled for substitute transportation options. The National Mediation Board, which governs labor relations for railroads, had stepped in to summon parties to negotiations in Manhattan.

articles.headline: US Premarket Movers for May 18, 2026
articles.summary: S&P 500 Index futures fell 0.4% as of 7:37 a.m. New York time on Monday as investors watched bond markets to see if Friday's surge in yields to multi-year highs would extend. The premarket session tracked the prior week's major bond selloff driven by accelerating inflation data and oil price gains tied to the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption. Bloomberg reported on the biggest US movers before the opening bell in a volatile market session dominated by energy and rate concerns.

articles.headline: US Premarket Movers for May 18, 2026
articles.summary: S&P 500 Index futures fell 0.4% as of 7:37 a.m. New York time on Monday as investors watched bond markets to see if Friday's surge in yields to multi-year highs would extend. The premarket session tracked the prior week's major bond selloff driven by accelerating inflation data and oil price gains tied to the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption. Bloomberg reported on the biggest US movers before the opening bell in a volatile market session dominated by energy and rate concerns.

articles.headline: US Lawmakers Plan New $130 Fee for Electric Vehicle Owners
articles.summary: House lawmakers released a massive $580 billion transportation bill Sunday that would impose new annual fees on electric and hybrid vehicles as gasoline prices surge following the Iran war. The bipartisan legislation, released by members of the House transportation committee, would impose an annual registration fee of $130 per electric vehicle, gradually rising biennially to $150, and as much as $50 for hybrids. The fees are intended to help fund the Highway Trust Fund as EV adoption reduces gasoline tax revenues. The legislation represents the first major federal transportation funding overhaul in years.

articles.headline: Kioxia's Booming Shares Head for Liquidity Boost With US Float
articles.summary: Kioxia Holdings Corp. announced plans to float American Depositary Shares on a US stock exchange, aiming to expand its investor base amid global fervor over memory chips. The Japanese chipmaker said in a release that the move would help raise corporate value, though details including the schedule and method remain undetermined and the company may not ultimately pursue the listing. ADSs would make shares directly available for trading, reducing arbitrage costs compared to depositary receipts that Kioxia already offers. The announcement positions Kioxia to capitalize on surging chip demand driven by AI infrastructure investment.

articles.headline: West Marine Files Chapter 11 Bankruptcy to Cut Debt, Close More Stores
articles.summary: Boating supply retailer West Marine Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 17 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, citing weaker sales as consumers pull back on outdoor recreation due to inflation and severe weather. The company reached a restructuring support agreement with 96.2% of term loan lenders, 100% of FILO lenders, and 93.9% of equity holders to either find a buyer or hand control to lenders owed $251 million. Approximately 200 stores across 34 states and Puerto Rico will remain open during restructuring. CEO Paulee Day said the company will "optimize our operations and rationalize our footprint" as part of the process.

articles.headline: Oil Climbs as Iran War Shows No Sign of Ending; Stocks Waver on Deal Doubts
articles.summary: Wall Street's rebound attempt failed Monday as oil rose after Iranian media reported fundamental differences remain in U.S.-Iran negotiations, with Tehran citing "excessive demands and unrealistic positions" in the latest U.S. draft proposal. U.S. crude topped $106 per barrel in volatile trading while Brent crude gained over 1.9% to $111.34 per barrel. The S&P 500 dropped 0.07% and the Nasdaq slid 0.51%, with traders monitoring oil prices and bond yields. President Trump warned Iran on Sunday that "the Clock is Ticking," adding to market anxiety over Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption.

articles.headline: China's Economy Loses Steam in April as Retail Sales Hit 40-Month Low
articles.summary: China's retail sales rose only 0.2% in April from a year ago, the weakest growth since December 2022, as the fallout from the Iran war dampened momentum in the world's second-largest economy. Industrial output climbed 4.1% in April, undershooting expectations for a 5.9% rise, while urban fixed asset investment contracted 1.6% against expectations for 1.6% growth. Crude oil refining volumes fell 5.8% from a year earlier, the steepest decline since August 2024. Following the Trump-Xi Beijing summit, China agreed to purchase at least $17 billion per year in U.S. agricultural products in 2026 through 2028, and an initial 200 jets from Boeing.

articles.headline: Pet Supplies Plus Franchisee PSP TS LLC Files Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
articles.summary: Florida-based Pet Supplies Plus franchisee PSP TS LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida in Tampa on May 12, listing $100,000 to $500,000 in assets and $1 million to $10 million in liabilities. The Holiday, Fla.-based franchisee's single Pet Supplies Plus store remains open, and the Pet Supplies Plus franchisor itself has not filed for bankruptcy. The Livonia, Mich.-based Pet Supplies Plus chain operates 725 locations in 44 states and 26 Wag N' Wash facilities nationwide. The debtor did not indicate a specific reason for the filing.

articles.headline: Industrial Realty Group Takes Portfolio Public
articles.summary: Los Angeles-based Industrial Realty Group is combining 98 industrial properties into a new publicly traded REIT through a definitive contribution agreement with Connecticut-based mortgage lender Sachem Capital Corp., creating IRG Realty Trust with an implied enterprise value of approximately $3.4 billion. The combined entity is expected to rank among the top 10 publicly listed industrial REITs by enterprise value, with IRG owning approximately 94.1% of the new company via operating partnership units and existing Sachem shareholders retaining roughly 5.9%. The 98 properties — described as mission-critical industrial infrastructure leased to manufacturing, distribution, and logistics tenants — carry a gross real estate asset value of $2.9 billion; Sachem's approximately $470 million in existing mortgage loan assets will also be included. The transaction, unanimously approved by Sachem's board, is expected to close by end of 2026 subject to Sachem shareholder approval, with Scotiabank advising IRG and Piper Sandler advising Sachem.

articles.headline: 2026 Iran war fuel crisis — Strait of Hormuz closure: ongoing global shipping and energy disruption
articles.source: Wikipedia (citing IEA, CRS, Dallas Fed, UNCTAD)
articles.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20% of global oil trade passes, has caused what the IEA characterized as the 'largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market.' Iranian forces declared the Strait closed beginning March 4, 2026, following the U.S.-Israeli Operation Epic Fury launched February 28; a brief reopening April 21–22 collapsed within 24 hours. Brent crude prices have exceeded $90 per barrel, container shipping companies including Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd suspended Mideast routes, and Asia-to-U.S. East Coast transpacific rates have climbed to approximately $3,800/FEU as of May 12, 2026, per SCFI data.

articles.headline: NerdWallet economic outlook week of May 18: Inflation risks tipping as CPI and PPI data signal continued price pressure
articles.summary: NerdWallet senior economist Elizabeth Renter noted that this week's CPI and PPI data signal risks tilting toward inflation, with the oil price shock described as 'significant, and only beginning.' Both sides of the Fed's dual mandate — stable prices and full employment — have been at risk, but current data show inflationary pressures strengthening. The U.S. trade deficit stood at $60.3 billion in March 2026, up 4.4% from February, with imports reaching $381.2 billion and exports $320.9 billion per BEA data.

articles.headline: Trump talks up trade deals with China, but experts see no big wins for U.S.
articles.summary: Analysts and former trade negotiators assessed the Trump-Xi Beijing summit as falling short of a major breakthrough despite White House claims of 'fantastic trade deals.' China agreed to purchase at least $17 billion in U.S. agricultural products over three years and restored market access for hundreds of U.S. beef facilities, according to the White House fact sheet. China also agreed to address U.S. access concerns for rare earths and other critical minerals, while industries have continued to struggle with supply shortages since Beijing postponed sweeping rare earth controls in October 2025. Boeing shares fell 3.8% on Friday, reflecting investor disappointment that the aircraft order of 200 jets was smaller than pre-summit expectations.

articles.headline: Everything's coming up roses: Flower wholesaler plants roots in Commerce with $34M acquisition
articles.summary: Holland Flower Market, a local importer and wholesaler of fresh-cut flowers, acquired a 91,010-square-foot industrial facility at 5555 East [address truncated in feed] in Commerce, California for $34 million. The acquisition represents an expansion of the company's footprint in the Los Angeles industrial corridor. The buyer is described as a local operator deepening its presence in the region with the larger warehouse.

articles.headline: At the Milken Institute Global Conference
articles.summary: The Milken Institute held its 29th annual Global Conference in Los Angeles amid persistent global economic volatility. The four-day event drew senior capital markets participants and functioned as a stress test of current economic conditions rather than a celebration of markets. Topics reportedly centered on navigating instability across global financial and business environments.

articles.headline: At the Milken Institute Global Conference
articles.summary: The Milken Institute held its 29th annual Global Conference in Los Angeles amid persistent global economic volatility. The four-day event drew senior capital markets participants and functioned as a stress test of current economic conditions rather than a celebration of markets. Topics reportedly centered on navigating instability across global financial and business environments.

articles.headline: CBB Folds in Bay-Area Lender
articles.summary: Ontario, California-based Citizens Business Bank completed a merger with Bay Area-based Heritage Bank of Commerce, pushing the regional lender's total assets above $20 billion. The deal represents Citizens Business Bank's largest acquisition to date. The merger extends the bank's geographic footprint into the Bay Area.

articles.headline: CBB Folds in Bay-Area Lender
articles.summary: Ontario, California-based Citizens Business Bank completed a merger with Bay Area-based Heritage Bank of Commerce, pushing the regional lender's total assets above $20 billion. The deal represents Citizens Business Bank's largest acquisition to date. The merger extends the bank's geographic footprint into the Bay Area.

articles.headline: Economic Outlook at Risk of Further Deterioration, OECD Says
articles.summary: OECD Secretary General Mathias Cormann, speaking on the sidelines of a Group of Seven meeting, said risks to the global economy have worsened as the conflict in the Middle East drags on. Cormann told Bloomberg Television that the ongoing war is 'putting downward pressure on growth and upward pressure on inflation.' He said the OECD provided an initial assessment in March and will revise it in the coming weeks. The comments came as G7 finance chiefs gathered to address a new economic reality shaped by energy disruption and rising bond yields.

articles.headline: EU Races to Finalize US Trade Deal to Avoid More Trump Tariffs
articles.summary: European Union officials met Tuesday in an effort to finalize legislation for the bloc's trade deal with the US, with failure to reach agreement risking the EU missing President Trump's July 4 deadline to have the accord in place. Trump previously threatened to hike tariffs on European auto imports to 25% from 15% because the EU had not moved quickly enough to implement the deal, which was signed nearly a year ago. The disagreement threatens to send transatlantic relations to a new low and trigger a fresh round of tariff escalation. The European Commission has said it maintains options to protect the bloc's interests if Trump follows through on the tariff threat.

articles.headline: Google, Blackstone to Create AI Cloud Company With In-House Chips
articles.summary: Alphabet's Google agreed to create an artificial intelligence cloud business with Blackstone Inc., aiming to compete with companies like CoreWeave in a burgeoning market. The project will rely on an initial $5 billion in equity capital from Blackstone, which will become the majority owner, with the total investment worth $25 billion including leverage. The joint venture will provide data center capacity, operations, networking, and Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units as a compute-as-a-service offering, with the first 500 megawatts of power expected online by 2027. The venture will be led by Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a veteran Google executive.

articles.headline: Trump to Swear In Warsh as Fed Chair on Friday, White House Confirms
articles.summary: Kevin Warsh will be sworn in as Federal Reserve chair by President Donald Trump on Friday during a ceremony at the White House, a White House official confirmed. Warsh will become the central bank's 17th leader, succeeding Jerome Powell, who has been serving in a temporary capacity after his official term ended last week. The US Senate confirmed Warsh earlier this month on a 54-45 vote, the slimmest confirmation margin ever for a Fed chair. Warsh takes the helm as the Fed faces elevated inflation driven by war-related energy price shocks and rising long-term Treasury yields.

articles.headline: Extended Oil Shock Spells Higher, Sticky Inflation
articles.summary: Bloomberg Television aired an analysis segment with Yelena Shulyatyeva, Senior US Economist at The Conference Board, examining the implications of a prolonged oil shock for inflation expectations. Shulyatyeva discussed the disconnect between inflation priced into 10-year Treasury yields and near-term market pricing for price rises. The analysis addressed whether elevated inflation is set to persist for an extended period or whether 10-year yields have moved beyond fundamentals. The segment aired as new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh prepares to take office amid back-to-back hot inflation data.

articles.headline: Google and Blackstone to Create New AI Cloud Company
articles.summary: Google and Blackstone plan to launch a new U.S.-based artificial intelligence cloud company using Google's specialized Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources. Blackstone, the world's largest alternative asset manager, will contribute an initial $5 billion in equity and hold a majority stake in the unnamed venture. Including leverage, the total investment value is expected to reach $25 billion. The venture aims to compete with companies like CoreWeave, with plans to bring 500 megawatts of data center capacity online in 2027.

articles.headline: Home Depot Reports Q1 Fiscal 2026 Results; Reaffirms Full-Year Guidance
articles.summary: Home Depot reported Q1 fiscal 2026 sales of $41.8 billion, up 4.8% from the same period a year earlier, beating analyst consensus estimates of approximately $41.5 billion. Net earnings were $3.3 billion, or $3.30 per diluted share, compared with $3.4 billion, or $3.45 per diluted share, in Q1 fiscal 2025; adjusted EPS came in at $3.43 versus $3.56 a year prior. Comparable sales increased 0.6% company-wide, with U.S. comps up 0.4%. The company reaffirmed its full-year fiscal 2026 guidance, calling for total sales growth of 2.5% to 4.5% and adjusted EPS growth of up to 4%.

articles.headline: Treasury Yields Near One-Year Highs as US-Iran Deal Uncertainty Persists
articles.summary: The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note hovered around 4.6% on Tuesday, pausing near one-year highs as renewed optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran agreement eased some inflation concerns. President Trump said he suspended a planned strike on Iran after appeals from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE, citing continued prospects for a deal. The 30-year Treasury bond yield remained elevated near 5.13%, and markets currently expect the Federal Reserve to leave the fed funds rate unchanged through year-end, though the implied probability of an additional 25 basis point rate hike has risen to approximately 40%. Investors are also awaiting the latest FOMC minutes and flash U.S. PMI data for additional clues on monetary policy and economic activity.

articles.headline: 2026 Strait of Hormuz Crisis — Wikipedia
articles.summary: Major container shipping companies including Maersk, CMA CGM, and Hapag-Lloyd suspended transits through the Strait of Hormuz and related routes including the Red Sea following the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran that began February 28. Brent crude oil prices surpassed $100 per barrel on March 8 and peaked at $126 per barrel, representing the largest monthly oil price increase on record. Iran on May 5 established the Persian Gulf Strait Authority to regulate maritime transit, and on May 13 an Indian-flagged cargo ship was struck by a projectile off the coast of Oman, indicating continued hostilities despite a temporary ceasefire. Houthi-controlled Yemen also resumed attacks on Red Sea commercial shipping, rerouting Suez Canal traffic around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.

articles.headline: $217 Million Just Hit the Table for Trucking Safety and CDL Development — Here's Who Can Apply and What It Means for Your Operation
articles.summary: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced on May 18 that the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is deploying $217 million across four grant programs targeting trucking safety enforcement, CDL program modernization, and technology deployment at roadside inspections. The funding represents a significant federal investment in commercial driver pipeline development and enforcement infrastructure. Motor carriers and CDL training programs are among the eligible applicants under the initiative.

articles.headline: Benchmark diesel down, futures market starts to tick upward
articles.summary: The benchmark price of diesel used for most fuel surcharge calculations declined in the latest weekly reading, according to FreightWaves. Despite the spot price drop, futures markets began moving upward during the same period. The divergence between current benchmark prices and forward-looking futures pricing signals potential near-term movement in carrier fuel surcharge rates.

articles.headline: Same Repair. Same Truck. Higher Invoice. Here Is the Number Behind What You Are Paying at the Parts Counter Right Now.
articles.summary: On October 17, 2025, President Trump signed a proclamation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, imposing a 25% tariff on imported medium and heavy-duty trucks and truck parts covering Class 3 through Class 8 vehicles, engines, and transmissions. The tariff has directly increased maintenance and repair costs for fleet operators purchasing parts at the counter. Trucking companies are absorbing higher per-unit parts costs on identical repairs compared to pre-tariff invoices.

articles.headline: 13,273 Trucks Got Parked During Blitz Week. If Your Violation Is Wrong, You Have a Real Way to Fight It.
articles.summary: The 2026 CVSA International Roadcheck ran May 12 through 14, with extended blitz-week enforcement spanning May 10 through 17. By the conclusion of the full enforcement period, 13,273 trucks were placed out of service, a figure larger than what the three-day Roadcheck event alone produced. The enforcement action represents a significant temporary reduction in available commercial truck capacity across affected corridors.

articles.headline: BNSF ops chief out after just five months
articles.summary: BNSF Railway has replaced its chief operating officer after Matt Garland held the position for only five months, according to FreightWaves. A new operations chief has taken over at the Class I railroad. No reason for Garland's departure was provided in the report.

articles.headline: Bankruptcy court approves STG Logistics reorganization plan
articles.summary: A federal bankruptcy court in New Jersey has approved the reorganization plan submitted by STG Logistics, according to FreightWaves. The court approval allows the logistics company to proceed with restructuring its operations and obligations under the plan. STG Logistics had been operating under bankruptcy protection prior to the court's ruling.

articles.headline: Roadcheck Week, Supreme Court ruling tighten US freight capacity
articles.summary: EASE Logistics reports that a combination of Roadcheck Week enforcement activity, insurance-related concerns stemming from a recent Supreme Court ruling, and seasonal freight demand are placing concurrent pressure on U.S. freight capacity. The factors are expected to sustain tightening conditions through the remainder of 2026. The Supreme Court ruling referenced relates to broker liability, which is affecting carrier availability and insurance underwriting in the spot market.

articles.headline: Is peak season here? Trans-Pacific rates level in latest week
articles.summary: Trans-Pacific ocean freight rates held steady in the latest weekly reading as the market approaches peak season, according to FreightWaves. Current rate levels reflect elevated fuel-cost baselines, with further shifts anticipated as seasonal cargo demand and fleet capacity management come into play. Liner operators are monitoring whether traditional peak season volume materializes to push rates higher.

articles.headline: Maersk back in the Red Sea: Drewry
articles.summary: Shipping consultant Drewry reports that Maersk has resumed transits through the Suez Canal-Red Sea route, leading a growing number of major carriers returning to the corridor. The move signals renewed confidence among brand-name vessel operators in the security conditions along the route. An increase in Red Sea transits by major liners could reduce transit times and affect global container supply chain routing patterns.

articles.headline: Target names former Walmart executive as chief supply chain officer
articles.summary: Target has hired Jeff England, a former Walmart executive most recently at QXO, as its new chief supply chain officer, according to FreightWaves. England will oversee Target's supply chain and logistics operations in the new role. The appointment represents a significant leadership change at one of the largest U.S. mass-market retailers.

articles.headline: New research: Tariffs didn't raise costs. They raised the execution standard.
articles.summary: New research cited by FreightWaves finds that the tariff environment that emerged in 2025 restructured U.S. trade by introducing duty brackets that did not exist in 2024, applying effective rates across multiple layered policies. The new rate structures collapsed cost predictability for importers managing large numbers of tariff line entries. The research frames the tariff impact less as a direct cost increase and more as a heightened operational and compliance execution requirement for trade professionals.

articles.headline: Senate approves Kloster for seat on Surface Transportation Board
articles.summary: The U.S. Senate has confirmed Richard Kloster to a seat on the Surface Transportation Board, according to the Journal of Commerce. Kloster joins the STB at a critical juncture as the agency reviews the proposed $85 billion merger of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The proposed combination would be the largest U.S. rail transaction in nearly three decades.

articles.headline: Senate approves Kloster for seat on Surface Transportation Board
articles.summary: The U.S. Senate has confirmed Richard Kloster to a seat on the Surface Transportation Board, according to the Journal of Commerce. Kloster joins the STB at a critical juncture as the agency reviews the proposed $85 billion merger of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The proposed combination would be the largest U.S. rail transaction in nearly three decades.

articles.headline: Ocean carriers face growing order book nearing 40% of in-service fleet
articles.summary: The ocean carrier industry faces an order book approaching 40% of the current in-service fleet, according to the Journal of Commerce. Liner executives contend that the surplus tonnage can be absorbed through a combination of vessel management practices, trade imbalances, increased scrapping activity, and continued geopolitical disruptions affecting route utilization. The scale of the pending capacity additions poses a structural challenge to freight rate sustainability across major trade lanes.

articles.headline: Mondelēz taps AI for distribution centers to cut costs
articles.summary: Mondelēz International is deploying artificial intelligence tools across its distribution centers with the objective of reducing operating costs, according to Supply Chain Dive. The snack and confectionery company is applying AI to distribution center operations as part of a broader cost-management initiative. The implementation reflects a growing adoption of AI-driven logistics optimization among large consumer packaged goods manufacturers.

articles.headline: Producer prices jump to 3-year high, spurred by war shortages
articles.summary: U.S. producer prices have risen to a three-year high, driven in part by supply shortages tied to the Iran war's impact on oil markets, according to Supply Chain Dive. The increase reflects upstream cost pressures working through supply chains as energy prices respond to geopolitical disruption. Elevated producer prices signal potential downstream cost increases for goods manufactured and distributed through industrial supply chains.

articles.headline: DavidsTea sets up US fulfillment after de minimis' end raises shipping hurdles
articles.summary: DavidsTea is establishing U.S.-based fulfillment operations following the end of the de minimis trade exemption, which CEO Sarah Segal said caused unpredictable delivery times and lower U.S. sales for the Canada-based tea company. The elimination of the de minimis rule raised cross-border shipping costs and complications for the direct-to-consumer retailer. Setting up domestic U.S. fulfillment is the company's operational response to the changed trade environment.

articles.headline: DC labor gets an AI boost
articles.summary: Warehouse managers in 2026 are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence tools to address challenges in storage, throughput, and fulfillment management amid elevated business uncertainty, according to DC Velocity. Geopolitical developments and tariff policy changes are cited as factors capable of triggering sudden demand surges that strain distribution center operations. AI-driven labor and workflow management systems are being positioned as solutions to improve operational flexibility under volatile conditions.

articles.headline: Locus Robotics acquires Nexera Robotics
articles.summary: Locus Robotics, a warehouse automation and autonomous mobile robot (AMR) company, has acquired Nexera Robotics, a Vancouver-based developer of advanced robotic grasping technology. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. The acquisition expands Locus Robotics' capabilities in warehouse automation with the addition of Nexera's grasping technology.

articles.headline: Santa Monica Airport – Grounded Future?
articles.summary: Businesses operating at Santa Monica Airport have launched a campaign opposing the planned closure of the airfield at the end of 2028. Tenants affected include flight schools, aircraft maintenance shops, nonprofit organizations, and a business incubator. The campaign seeks to head off the shutdown, which would displace scores of commercial operators currently based at the airport.

articles.headline: Retail market stays up, defying economic headwinds
articles.summary: U.S. retail sales rose for the seventh consecutive month in April, according to the National Retail Federation, despite high gas prices and inflation. Nationwide sales, excluding automobile and gasoline transactions, increased 0.34 percent from March. The consecutive monthly gains signal continued consumer spending activity across the retail sector.

articles.headline: Long Bond Yields Climb to 17-Year High as Investors React to Inflation Concerns
articles.summary: Yields on the US Treasury's longest-dated bond rose to the highest level in almost two decades as investor concern over accelerating inflation fueled a selloff across global debt markets. The 30-year yield rose as much as seven basis points to 5.19% on Tuesday, reaching a level last seen on the eve of the 2007 global financial crisis. Bond markets across Europe and Asia also fell, while the selloff spilled over into US equity markets. Oil holding above $100 and no signs of an end to the Iran conflict drove the yield surge, amid concern that elevated energy costs are increasing the chances the next Federal Reserve move will be a hike, not a cut.

articles.headline: Bond Yields Near Two-Decade High Open Rift Among Investors
articles.summary: A surge in longer-maturity US Treasury yields is testing the resolve of global bond investors torn between locking in rates near the highest levels in decades and the risk of an even greater selloff. With Treasury 30-year yields near the highest since 2007, a Goldman Sachs team sees some emerging value but urges caution. Barclays and Citigroup strategists are warning clients yields may breach 5.5%, levels last seen in 2004. The head of BlackRock's research unit is recommending investors reduce their exposure to developed-market government bonds, including Treasuries, in favor of equities.

articles.headline: Citi Says 5.5% May Be Next Focus for 30-Year Treasury Yield
articles.summary: Bond traders are zeroing in on 5.5% as the new benchmark level for 30-year US Treasury yields as inflation concerns ripple across markets, according to Citigroup. Citigroup's London-based macro rates strategist Jim McCormick said the focus is likely to shift to this level after long-end yields climbed to 5.16% this week, approaching the highest since 2007. The last time 30-year yields hit 5.5% was 22 years ago. The move reflects sustained inflation fears tied to the ongoing Iran war and elevated energy costs.

articles.headline: Global Inflation Weighs on G-7 as Higher Bond Yields Persist
articles.summary: Global finance chiefs gathering in Paris for a two-day G-7 meeting are coming to terms with the reality that a consumer-price shock is looking likely to endure. On the second day of Group of Seven discussions, the aftermath of a bond-market readjustment factoring in more inflation has raised the burden of proof needed to keep borrowing costs unchanged. The prospect of higher interest rates is looming, with associated stress to growth and budget deficits. Finance ministers and central bankers are preoccupied with another day of spiking yields driven by investor concerns about consumer prices.

articles.headline: Bond Yield Surge Poses Threat to Asia's AI-Fueled Stock Rally
articles.summary: Rising US bond yields pose a threat to Asia's stock rally, as growing inflation fears offset ongoing optimism over benefits from the artificial intelligence boom. Over the past five years, the MSCI Asia Pacific Index has fallen in 16 of the 19 weeks when the US 10-year Treasury yield rose by 20 basis points or more, losing 1.6% on average, according to Bloomberg data. Last week followed that pattern as yields surged on Iran war inflation concerns. The risk-off dynamic in global markets is creating fresh headwinds for capital flows into emerging Asian equities.

articles.headline: NY's LIRR Resumes Train Service After Labor Deal to End Strike
articles.summary: The Long Island Rail Road resumed initial service after the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and several labor unions reached a tentative deal to end a three-day strike. The first LIRR trains began running at noon on Tuesday on four of the commuter rail's branches, with the MTA expecting full operations by the evening. The tentative deal between the MTA and five unions on wage increases was announced by New York Governor Kathy Hochul late Monday. The strike was the first LIRR walkout since a two-day strike in 1994, involving 3,500 engineers, signalmen, and electrical workers.

articles.headline: New York's LIRR Trains Set to Restart Tuesday After Strike Deal
articles.summary: New York City's transit system and Long Island Rail Road workers reached a potential labor agreement, ending a historic strike that suspended service on the largest commuter rail line in the US. The tentative deal between the MTA and five unions on wage increases was announced by Governor Kathy Hochul late Monday. The MTA had warned that union demands would require fare increases and set a difficult precedent for negotiations with other transit unions. The deal still requires ratification by rank-and-file members of the five unions that went on strike.

articles.headline: UP CEO confident rail merger application checks all the STB's boxes
articles.summary: Union Pacific CEO expressed confidence that the revised UP-Norfolk Southern merger application meets all requirements set by the Surface Transportation Board. The application has been resubmitted following earlier review. No timeline for STB action was specified in the report.

articles.headline: Target moves to elevate supply chain operations, inventory reliability
articles.summary: Target has identified supply chain improvement as a strategic priority, aiming to eliminate out-of-stock situations and reduce operational costs. The retailer is investing in supply chain operations to improve inventory reliability across its network. The initiative reflects ongoing efforts by major retailers to strengthen distribution and fulfillment capabilities.

articles.headline: DoJ indicts Chinese container makers on price-fixing charges
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted four major Chinese shipping container manufacturers and seven individual executives on charges related to a global price-fixing conspiracy. The indictments target some of the world's largest box manufacturers. The action follows other U.S. measures against Chinese logistics and port equipment firms, including reciprocal port fees and tariffs.

articles.headline: Another CA truck crash and two dead kids on Highway 99
articles.summary: A Freightliner Cascadia operated by Amritsar Trans Inc., a five-truck carrier based in Manteca, California, rear-ended three vehicles on Highway 99 near Lodi on May 19, 2026, killing two young men. The driver fled the scene on foot following the collision. The carrier is described as operating within a broader web of compliance concerns.

articles.headline: Rail on a roll as ag, metals, chemicals lead traffic
articles.summary: U.S. rail freight volumes posted another positive week, with seven out of 10 commodity categories showing year-over-year improvement. Agricultural products, metals, and chemicals led traffic gains during the reporting period. The data reflects continued broad-based strength in rail freight demand.

articles.headline: 79 ELDs revoked since January. 12 more just hit the list.
articles.summary: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration removed 12 additional electronic logging devices from its registered device list, bringing the total number of revocations to 79 since January 2025. The pace of removals is outstripping the rate at which new devices are being added to the registry. The trend raises questions about the agency's longer-term direction on ELD oversight.

articles.headline: RXO sees TL spot market surge further in Q2
articles.summary: Freight broker RXO reported better-than-expected spot market conditions in the second quarter of 2026, with truckload spot rates surging beyond earlier projections. The company indicated that Q2 trends are tracking above internal forecasts. The development signals improving freight demand conditions in the broader truckload market.

articles.headline: Evolution of ocean capacity linked to varied dynamics of trade needs
articles.summary: The alignment between ocean freight demand and vessel capacity supply varies significantly across individual trade lanes, according to an analysis by Jeremy Masters. These dynamics carry different consequences for the newbuild, second-hand, and charter vessel markets. The piece examines how trade-lane-specific conditions are shaping carrier capacity deployment decisions.

articles.headline: US move against container makers is latest entry in logistics battle with China
articles.summary: The Justice Department's indictments against four major Chinese container manufacturers are the latest in a series of U.S. actions targeting Chinese dominance in logistics infrastructure. Prior measures have included reciprocal port fees and tariffs on China-made port equipment. The indictments allege a global price-fixing conspiracy involving the box manufacturers and multiple executives.

articles.headline: Zim reports Q1 loss, with bunker impact expected to worsen in Q2
articles.summary: Zim Integrated Shipping Services reported a net loss in the first quarter of 2026, with CEO Eli Glickman citing war-driven oil price increases as a significant drag on results. Glickman warned that bunker fuel costs are expected to weigh more heavily on the company's financials in the second quarter. Zim declined to offer earnings guidance, citing the pending merger with Hapag-Lloyd.

articles.headline: Spot rate surge may signal early peak season on trans-Pacific
articles.summary: Trans-Pacific spot and FAK freight rates have surged, with some analysts suggesting the move may indicate an earlier-than-usual peak shipping season. The strength of any peak remains uncertain, with blank sailings, fuel-linked surcharges, and the annual service contract changeover all contributing to upward rate pressure. The underlying demand drivers have not been fully established.

articles.headline: Matson reports air-to-ocean freight conversions amid Iran war
articles.summary: U.S.-based ocean carrier Matson reported observing a shift in shipper behavior, with customers converting air freight shipments to ocean freight amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. The carrier linked the trend to disruptions and cost pressures affecting air cargo routing. Matson's comments provide insight into how the Iran conflict is influencing shipper modal decisions.

articles.headline: Danone to close plant-based dairy facility in New Jersey
articles.summary: Danone announced plans to close a plant-based dairy manufacturing facility in New Jersey that produces its Silk and So Delicious brands. The closure represents a reduction in the company's North American manufacturing footprint for plant-based products. Danone has not disclosed the number of workers affected or a specific timeline for the shutdown.

articles.headline: EU lawmakers back US trade pact with built-in safeguards
articles.summary: The European Parliament has voted to support a trade agreement with the United States that includes built-in safeguard mechanisms. The pact is designed to govern tariff and trade flow conditions between the EU and the U.S. Specific terms of the safeguards and the timeline for ratification were not detailed in the available description.

articles.headline: Muted peak season expected as ocean shippers delay contract signing
articles.summary: Ocean shippers are delaying the signing of annual contracts amid market uncertainty, contributing to expectations of a muted peak shipping season. The hesitation reflects broader uncertainty about trade volumes and freight rate direction heading into the second half of the year. The delay in contract commitments signals that shippers are opting for flexibility over locked-in rates as conditions remain unpredictable.

articles.headline: Up, up, and (put)away
articles.summary: Warehouses and distribution centers are facing sustained pressure to accommodate growing inventory volumes, more SKUs, higher order counts, and increased shipments. Expanding existing building footprints is not always feasible, prompting operators to explore alternative strategies for capacity growth. The article examines approaches facilities are taking to maximize throughput within constrained physical footprints.

articles.headline: Insurance cost increases outpace consumer inflation, trucking industry report shows
articles.summary: Trucking industry insurance premiums are rising at a rate more than five percentage points above consumer inflation, according to a new report from the American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI). The report, focused on trucking industry costs, highlights insurance as a growing financial burden for carriers. ATRI's data underscores the widening gap between general inflation and sector-specific cost pressures facing motor carriers.

articles.headline: LA County brings Palisades, Eaton fire recovery efforts under one roof with new agency
articles.summary: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted Tuesday to establish a new agency dedicated to coordinating long-term recovery efforts from the January 2025 Palisades and Eaton fires. The agency is designed to streamline the rebuilding process by consolidating bureaucratic functions that have historically slowed post-disaster reconstruction. The move formalizes the county's recovery apparatus as rebuilding efforts in affected communities continue.

articles.headline: LA County's post-fire rent gouging ban goes up in smoke
articles.summary: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors failed to secure the votes necessary to extend an emergency anti-price gouging ban on rents that was enacted following the January 2025 wildfires. The expiration of the ban will give landlords greater pricing flexibility in a rental market still affected by fire-related displacement. The vote outcome means tenant protections tied to the disaster declaration will lapse.

articles.headline: Onni's $400M loan finds itself in special servicing again
articles.summary: Onni Group's $408 million loan secured by Wilshire Courtyard has been transferred to special servicing, according to Morningstar Credit. The approximately one-million-square-foot Miracle Mile office complex is located at 5700 to 5750 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles. Onni currently owes approximately $384 million on the loan, and the servicer has been engaged to manage the distressed debt situation.

articles.headline: Fed Minutes Show More Officials Warned of Rate-Hike Scenario
articles.summary: A majority of Federal Reserve officials warned the central bank would likely need to consider raising interest rates if inflation continued to run persistently above their 2% target, according to minutes of the April 28–29 FOMC meeting. Many officials called for the Fed to drop its easing bias and signal its next move could be a rate increase. The April meeting featured four dissenting votes — the most since 1992 — with three members objecting to language implying future cuts remain the base case. The minutes were released as incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prepares to be sworn in, and markets are now pricing roughly a 39% probability of a rate hike by year-end.

articles.headline: Bond Yield Spike: What It Means for Economies and Markets
articles.summary: A prolonged period of elevated long-term bond yields is ramping up borrowing costs around the world, as investors demand more compensation for holding government debt following the Iran war's ignition of fresh inflation fears. Yields on 30-year US Treasuries have risen above 5% to the highest since 2007, while equivalent UK debt is yielding the most in almost three decades. The rate on 20-year Japanese bonds is the highest since 1996. The global bond selloff reflects compounding concerns over public debt levels, central bank rate paths, and sustained energy-driven inflation.

articles.headline: Bond Yields Are Rising for Reasons Both Benign and Concerning
articles.summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist and former New York Fed President Bill Dudley writes that yields on 10-year Treasury notes have risen nearly half a percentage point to just under 4.70% this week — the highest since January 2025. Dudley identifies three cyclical drivers: stronger-than-anticipated economic growth, sustained consumer spending despite energy and tariff shocks, and a surge in business investment led by AI infrastructure buildout. Expectations for monetary policy have shifted from rate cuts to potential increases, with prevailing market wisdom now pointing toward tightening rather than easing.

articles.headline: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P Live Updates for May 21
articles.summary: A US–Iran standoff over key peace deal terms lifted oil prices on May 21, dragging down stocks and bonds on concern that a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure could worsen energy disruptions and fuel inflation. While Tehran said the latest Washington proposal had partly bridged the gap between the two sides, a report that Iran plans to retain its near-weapons-grade uranium was seen as a potential setback. The S&P 500 erased its week-to-date gain, and US crude topped $101 per barrel, driving Treasury yields higher on fears the Fed will be forced to raise rates.

articles.headline: Repeat After Me, Stocks Are Not an Effective Inflation Hedge
articles.summary: Bloomberg analysis reports that investors are piling into equities even as they anticipate rising inflation, a strategy Bloomberg argues is likely to backfire. Inflation is described as resurgent as the energy shock from the Iran war ripples through the global economy. The net percentage of respondents in Bank of America's Fund Manager Survey expecting higher inflation is back at its highest level since the pandemic. The piece urges investors to refocus on real economic quantities rather than nominal equity values.

articles.headline: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for May 21
articles.summary: Oil prices inched higher after plummeting on Wednesday, as President Trump said the US is in the "final stages" of negotiations with Iran. Brent crude was above $105 per barrel after sliding 5.6% the prior session, while West Texas Intermediate traded near $99. Trump's comments to reporters stoked hopes for a deal between Washington and Tehran that would see a near-term restart of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Price volatility is directly tied to the status of peace negotiations and their potential effect on global oil supply.

articles.headline: Euro-Area Output Falls Sharply, Raising Risks for Growth and Inflation
articles.summary: Business activity in the euro area shrank at the quickest pace in 2½ years in May, adding to fears that the Iran war and accompanying surge in energy costs are dealing a severe blow to the economy. The Composite Purchasing Managers' Index compiled by S&P Global fell to 47.5 in May from 48.8 in April, holding below the 50-point expansion threshold for a second consecutive month. Bloomberg survey analysts had anticipated an unchanged reading. The sharper-than-expected contraction compounds inflation concerns and raises questions about the ECB's monetary policy path.

articles.headline: ICE Raids Did Lasting Damage to American Businesses
articles.summary: Bloomberg's data-driven investigation finds that foot traffic and sales in a Charlotte, North Carolina immigrant business corridor remain depressed six months after the Department of Homeland Security's Operation Charlotte's Web deportation raids in November 2025. The analysis documents measurable, persistent economic decline in a one-mile stretch of Central Avenue filled with immigrant-owned businesses. The report is part of Bloomberg's broader coverage of the microeconomic consequences of federal immigration enforcement for bellwether firms. The findings illustrate how enforcement operations are creating lasting demand destruction in specific labor and consumer markets relevant to industrial tenant operating conditions.

articles.headline: Anthropic Revenue Surges, Set to Post First Profit
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal was first to report that Anthropic has told investors it expects Q2 revenue of $10.9 billion — a 130% increase over Q1's $4.8 billion — which would surpass the company's total 2025 annual sales. The company projects an operating profit of $559 million for the June quarter, which would mark its first profitable quarter since founding in 2021. The figures were shared with investors as part of an ongoing funding round that could push Anthropic's valuation above OpenAI's. Anthropic does not expect sustained profitability throughout the full year due to substantial upcoming compute infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Walmart Posts Strong Q1 Results But Cautious Guidance Rattles Investors
articles.summary: Walmart reported Q1 FY27 net sales of $175.7 billion, topping the $174.8 billion analyst consensus, with e-commerce sales up 26% globally and Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth of 4.1%. The company reported adjusted EPS of $0.66, matching Wall Street forecasts, with net income of $5.33 billion. Executives left full-year FY27 guidance unchanged and warned that persistently high fuel costs — driven by the U.S.-Iran war's disruption of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic — would increasingly pressure store prices and consumer spending in Q2. Walmart's stock fell approximately 7% on the day as investors reacted to the flat guidance and fuel cost warnings.

articles.headline: Walmart Posts Strong Q1 Results But Cautious Guidance Rattles Investors
articles.summary: Walmart reported Q1 FY27 net sales of $175.7 billion, topping the $174.8 billion analyst consensus, with e-commerce sales up 26% globally and Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth of 4.1%. The company reported adjusted EPS of $0.66, matching Wall Street forecasts, with net income of $5.33 billion. Executives left full-year FY27 guidance unchanged and warned that persistently high fuel costs — driven by the U.S.-Iran war's disruption of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic — would increasingly pressure store prices and consumer spending in Q2. Walmart's stock fell approximately 7% on the day as investors reacted to the flat guidance and fuel cost warnings.

articles.headline: SpaceX Is Aiming to Go Public on June 12, Setting the Stage for What Is Expected to Be the Biggest IPO of All Time
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX is targeting a June 12 Nasdaq listing under the ticker SPCX, with pricing expected June 11 and a formal roadshow beginning June 4. The company is seeking to raise approximately $75 billion at a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion, which would make it the largest IPO on record, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut. Goldman Sachs is leading the offering alongside Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup, and JPMorgan. The S-1 prospectus, filed with the SEC in April, discloses combined SpaceX-xAI 2025 revenue of $18.67 billion following SpaceX's all-stock acquisition of xAI in February 2026.

articles.headline: West Marine Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy, Plans to Rationalize Its Store Footprint
articles.summary: West Marine, the largest U.S. boating and marine supplies retailer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on May 17, 2026. The company secured a Restructuring Support Agreement backed by 96.2% of its term loan lenders, 100% of its FILO lenders, and 93.9% of equity holders, with secured lenders also committing to new exit financing. West Marine's approximately 200 retail locations across 34 states and Puerto Rico will remain open during the restructuring, with the company stating it intends to 'optimize operations and rationalize its footprint.' The company's largest unsecured creditor is Garmin International at $8.57 million, followed by distribution logistics company Virtual Supply Inc. at $5.8 million. Portage Point Partners is serving as investment banker.

articles.headline: CoStar World News for May 21
articles.summary: CoStar's daily international news digest for May 21 covers global CRE investment trends. French non-traded REIT fundraising increased 10% year-over-year to €1.2 billion in Q1 2026, with diversified funds accounting for 72% of inflows; logistics and industrial captured 3% of total investment inflows. The roundup also includes German residential debt issuance, Toronto investment market data showing a $3.4 billion year-over-year gain in aggregate investment volume, and retail market analysis from a JLL report presented at ICSC's Las Vegas conference.

articles.headline: How The Wonderful Logistics Center Is Transforming California's Central Valley
articles.summary: The Wonderful Company's Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter, California is a 2,000-acre, fully entitled and master-planned logistics development featuring more than 17 million square feet of space currently in operation, with over 10,000 careers created since opening. Wonderful Real Estate, a division of The Wonderful Company, is developing three business parks totaling 1,865 acres in California's Central Valley, with multiple properties already leased or purchased by Fortune 500 companies. The article notes the U.S. industrial market posted 40 million square feet of net absorption in Q1 2026, its best quarterly result in three years, with tenants increasingly seeking newer warehouse products capable of supporting automation, AI systems, and higher power requirements. The article was produced in collaboration with BisNow's Studio B content studio.

articles.headline: US-China Tariff Rates: Where Things Stand as of May 20, 2026
articles.summary: China and the US appear to have agreed on terms for restoration of US tariffs on Chinese goods through Section 301 investigations, following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, though no extension to the one-year trade truce through November 2026 has been finalized. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on May 19 that he believes China will accept restoration of prior tariff rates 'as long as they don't go higher,' with the two Section 301 investigations set to conclude this summer. The effective tariff rate on many Chinese goods shipped to the US remains close to 30%, still the highest of any country, reflecting a 15% global tariff in effect since February 24, 2026 plus surviving Section 232 and Section 301 duties. Section 301 tariff exclusions for 178 products have been extended until November 10, 2026.

articles.headline: Motor Carriers Game Out USMCA Futures Ahead of July 1 Deadline
articles.summary: Motor carriers across North America are adjusting investment and network decisions as the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement enters its first mandatory review ahead of a July 1 milestone, with initial US-Mexico talks starting the week of May 25. Carriers say prolonged uncertainty, not border disruption, risks chilling investment and capacity planning in an already fragile freight market. The three countries must decide by July 1 whether to extend USMCA for 16 years or begin annual reviews that could lead to expiration by 2036. TFI International Chairman Alain Bédard told analysts the uncertainty is too high to make major capital commitments until the agreement's future is clarified.
